objects.original: An arbitrary Riemannian submanifold M of finite-dimensional Euclidean E, smooth manifold objective F, any smooth neighborhood extension f, and the Riemannian gradient grad F characterized as a tangent vector field. The original includes sphere tangent context.
objects.reconstructed: The unit sphere S in a finite-dimensional real inner-product E, total ambient f, genuine ambient gradient witness g at x, abstract chart tangent w and ambient tangent candidate z in L=(R x) orthogonal complement. No chosen manifold gradient field is defined.
objects.evidence: Reconstruction accurately expands the Lean carriers; it is a source-present sphere specialization, but has neither arbitrary M nor a globally defined smooth gradient field.

domains.original: M ranges over Riemannian submanifolds of Euclidean E, with exactly the induced metric. Ambient extension is defined on any neighborhood U of M; source tangent vectors are embedded in E. Sphere is one particular example.
domains.reconstructed: M is fixed to Metric.sphere 0 1. dim E=n+1 for n natural, including n=0; f:E→R is total. w lives in actual TangentSpace(𝓡 n)x and z in ambient orthogonal subspace L.
domains.evidence: The full arbitrary-manifold domain is absent. For the source sphere example, finrank typing entails no extra nonempty-point restriction: x on a unit sphere already forces nonzero ambient dimension. Given a source smooth extension on open U containing S, a total function equal to it on U and arbitrary outside U has the same local derivative and sphere restriction; no globally smooth total extension is claimed.

quantifiers.original: For any induced-metric Riemannian submanifold M, smooth F and smooth neighborhood extension f, the pointwise gradient formula holds at every x and is characterized against every embedded tangent v.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every E,n,x,f,g satisfying ambient HasGradientAt at x, and every ambient tangent candidate z, all abstract chart tangent w pair correctly iff z is the projection of g.
quantifiers.evidence: Universality over arbitrary M is lost. Universality over x and all test directions is preserved on sphere instances. The candidate iff makes source uniqueness explicit; source arbitrary extensions can be specialized locally, but neither arbitrary extension construction nor general-manifold quantification is supplied.

assumptions.original: Finite Euclidean carrier, embedded Riemannian submanifold with induced metric, globally smooth F and a smooth extension to a neighborhood.
assumptions.reconstructed: FiniteDimensional real inner-product carrier, sphere dimension typing and x in sphere, only pointwise HasGradientAt f g x. Actual inclusion differentiability/range are internally proved library inputs, not extra premises.
assumptions.evidence: For the selected sphere geometry, source smoothness implies a genuine pointwise derivative represented by its Euclidean gradient. Pointwise HasGradientAt does not imply source global smoothness; this is an explicit valid generalization, not literal assumption equivalence or a source correction. There are no convenience metric/differential/pairing hypotheses.

conclusion.original: grad_M F(x)=Proj_x grad_E f(x) for arbitrary induced-metric submanifolds, with grad F the uniquely characterized Riemannian gradient.
conclusion.reconstructed: On the sphere only, z represents the genuine restricted manifold differential through <dι_x w,z> iff z=P_Lg; setting z=P_Lg yields unique existence of that ambient representative.
conclusion.evidence: The sphere iff faithfully realizes the pointwise source characterization after actual inclusion identification. The whole arbitrary-manifold conclusion is unproved. A gradient object on abstract TangentSpace, global metric structure, or smooth gradient field is not a conclusion of this declaration.

The source names a general gradient vector field; Lean constructs only a local sphere ambient representative. Global metric/gradient-field and general well-definedness construction are not discharged. This is a full-source fidelity boundary, not a mathematical defect in the sphere theorem.

Source embedded tangent v corresponds to A_x w, the actual inclusion differential applied to an abstract chart tangent direction. Exact range gives all source directions; injectivity supports induced pullback metric interpretation. Candidate z is ambient tangent, not identified with abstract tangent by an unstated equality.

Lean f is total; a source neighborhood extension gives the same local instance by taking a total function agreeing on its open domain and arbitrary outside. No smooth extension construction/global smooth total map is claimed.
